messages:
Anya K: FYI we're getting a p95 spike between GPU nodes in pool-3 during the midday batch ramp (12:05-12:20). Alerts just hit the SLO dashboard :eyes:
ops-bot: [ALERT] interconnect-p95 > 250ms on cluster/gpu-pool-3 (12:06) — triggered by service: serving-runtime, route: /generate
Anya K: Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/xyz/ew-latency — you'll see the tight spike that matches the batch window. Looks like 12:05–12:18 each host pair ramps up and p95 jumps ~2-3x
Rajesh N: Can you paste the ib/eth counters from one of the affected nodes? specifically: ethtool -S, ibv_devinfo and rdma counters
Marta SRE: grabbing now, one host (gpu-03-21) shows retransmits and some rcv_errors. quick dump:
```
# ibv_devinfo -v mlx5_0
port: 1
  state: ACTIVE (4)
  phys_state: LINK_UP
  link_layer: InfiniBand
  port_rcv_errors: 482
  port_xmit_discards: 3
  port_xmit_data: 1.2T
# cat /sys/class/infiniband/mlx5_0/counters/retry_cnt
retry_cnt: 124
# ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'rx_errors|tx_errors|rx_no_buffer'
rx_errors: 0
tx_errors: 1
rx_no_buffer: 0
```
Rajesh N: retry_cnt that high looks like link-layer retries, not TCP drops. Could be RDMA link flapping / congestion. Any recent NIC FW or kernel updates?
Devon R: We rolled the serving-runtime continuous-batching tweak yesterday to reduce cold token overhead (batch window slightly larger, more aggressive coalesce). That increases simultaneous flows across peerlinks — could amplify congestion tails.
Anya K: Also noticed these spikes align with a specific rack subset (rack-3a). Not cluster-wide. Could be a path issue or local fabric QP contention.
Marta SRE: I ran a tcpdump on veth->eth0 during a spike, not many TCP retrans, mostly stalled application-level ACKs while RDMA retries climb. snippet: ``ibcounters: retry increase starts at 12:06:07 then p95 jumps``
Rajesh N: Two suspects: MTU mismatch or buffer pressure (GRO/GSO/GSOv4 offload interaction) on the ToR->GPU host path. Also verify PKey/MTU across switches. Can you check `ip -s link show` and switch MTU config for rack-3a?
Anya K: ip -s link show on gpu-03-21: 
```
3: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes 1.1T  packets 12.3M  errors 0  dropped 0
    TX: bytes 1.0T  packets 11.9M  errors 1  dropped 0
```
Switch team confirmed MTU 9000 everywhere on that path. No obvious mismatch.
Devon R: If MTU checks out, could be an interrupt/coalescing or QP exhaustion case when batch concurrency spikes. We increased default QPs per pod in the batch tuning patch (PR #412). Maybe we overcommitted QPs on those hosts.
Marta SRE: I see K8s pod density on gpu-03-21 is higher today (extra canary pods). Combined with larger batch windows that could push many concurrent RDMA sessions.
Rajesh N: Quick mitigation options: 1) throttle batch concurrency per-node (runtime config) 2) move some pods off rack-3a (drain) 3) enable per-path pacing on ToR (if available) 4) rollback the batch window change (last resort)
Anya K: Let's do a quick mitigation: reduce runtime batching concurrency on pool-3 by 30% and observe. Can someone patch config and roll in canary?
Devon R: On it. Will flip `max_concurrent_batches` from 80 -> 55 for pool-3 and do a rolling config push to one AZ first.
Marta SRE: I'll start moving two canary pods off gpu-03-21 to spread the QP load after the config change.
ops-bot: [INFO] config-deploy started: serving-runtime/pool-3 (change: max_concurrent_batches=55)
Rajesh N: While this runs, please collect detailed IB counters across affected hosts for the past 24h (retry_cnt, rnr_nak, path_mtu_errors). We should also take switch telemetry for rack-3a around the spike windows.
Anya K: Agreed. Also scheduling NIC FW audit for rack-3a tonight — no rollouts without SRE/Net signoff.
Devon R: Canary config pushed to az-a, p95 dropped from ~290ms -> ~120ms on the canary subset within one batch window. Looks promising :thumbsup:
Marta SRE: After moving pods and canary pushing, gpu-03-21 retry_cnt growth stalled and p95 reduced. Still a few hosts with residual retries, but nothing SLO-breaking.
Rajesh N: Good. Root-cause follow-ups: correlate QP counts + pod count + batch concurrency to identify safe defaults. Also escalate to infra for deeper fabric counters (switch queue drops) and check for any intermittent ToR fabric errors.
Anya K: Action items: 1) Devon to propose new max_concurrent_batches per pool (due EOD) 2) Rajesh to collect switch telemetry + RDMA counters for rack-3a (due tomorrow AM) 3) Marta to finish spreading pods and monitor for 24h 4) Ops to audit NIC FW on rack-3a (tonight).
Devon R: I'll open an RFC with the proposed tuning matrix and include backtest results from canary.
Marta SRE: Marking this thread resolved for now, will re-open if p95 rebounds. Thanks team :heart:
Anya K: Nice work — the quick throttle bought us time to avoid a rollback. Follow-ups as above.
